content.user_title: Analyze Logs for Errors and Incidents
content.value_statement: Logs hide errors, slow requests, and suspicious access patterns across many files. This skill guides read-only searches that summarize causes, trends, and response actions.
actual_capabilities: Locate common system, web server, and application log paths.
Search logs for errors, exceptions, failures, and HTTP 4xx or 5xx responses.
Group log activity by time window, IP address, endpoint, or request count.
Review response times and identify slow requests in access logs.
Flag suspicious patterns such as SQL injection, XSS, traversal, and brute force attempts.
Produce a concise report with summary, counts, tables, and recommended actions.
limitations: Depends on the log files and formats available in the workspace.
Does not change logs or perform incident remediation by itself.
Cannot verify root cause without application, infrastructure, or deployment context.
Sensitive values must be masked before sharing findings outside the team.

use_cases.title: Debug Production Errors
use_cases.description: Find recent errors, count repeated failures, and connect timestamps with likely causes.

use_cases.title: Investigate Traffic Spikes
use_cases.description: Review request volume, top IPs, endpoints, and slow responses during a service incident.

use_cases.title: Review Security Signals
use_cases.description: Search access logs for suspicious patterns and prepare a clean investigation summary.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the available application logs for recent ERROR, exception, and failure messages. Summarize the top patterns, counts, timestamps, and likely next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review HTTP Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect access logs for HTTP 4xx and 5xx responses in the requested time window. Group results by endpoint, status code, and source IP.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Performance Hotspots
prompt_templates.prompt: Review access logs for slow requests, high-volume endpoints, and latency outliers. Include request examples, counts, and time ranges.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Suspicious Activity
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze logs for SQL injection, XSS, directory traversal, and login brute force patterns. Mask sensitive values and list evidence by timestamp and source.

output_examples.input: Investigate an error spike in application logs around 14:00 UTC.
output: Summary of the analysis window, total lines reviewed, and error count.
Top repeated error patterns with first seen and last seen times.
Recommended checks for the service owner and deployment history.

output_examples.input: Review access logs for slow requests and traffic changes.
output: List of slowest request paths with counts and representative timestamps.
Request volume grouped by minute and endpoint.
Notes on possible bottlenecks and follow-up metrics to compare.

output_examples.input: Search access logs for suspicious login and injection activity.
output: Grouped suspicious patterns by source, endpoint, and time range.
Masked evidence examples that avoid exposing secrets or personal data.
Suggested containment and review steps for the security team.

best_practices: Set a clear time window and timezone before comparing log entries.
Mask passwords, tokens, email addresses, and session values in shared reports.
Compare errors with deployments, infrastructure events, and traffic changes.
anti_patterns: Running broad searches without a time window on very large logs.
Sharing raw log excerpts that include secrets or personal data.
Treating repeated errors as root cause without checking surrounding context.

faq.question: What log types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports application logs, Apache logs, Nginx logs, JSON logs, and common system log locations.

faq.question: Does it modify log files?
faq.answer: No. The workflow is designed for read-only inspection and reporting.

faq.question: Can it find security anomalies?
faq.answer: Yes. It searches for injection attempts, traversal patterns, brute force activity, and unusual access volume.

faq.question: Does it handle sensitive log data?
faq.answer: It instructs users to mask passwords, tokens, and other sensitive values before sharing results.

faq.question: Can it analyze compressed logs?
faq.answer: It reminds users to include rotated or compressed logs when they are relevant to the incident window.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the log location, time range, timezone, system context, and the incident symptoms you want reviewed.
